```python
import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 12
    n_vehicles = 3
    Q = 95  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[81, 75], [84, 59], [15, 71], [38, 72], [52, 68], [59, 45], [29, 9], [42, 11], [27, 21], [24, 47], [56, 29], [86, 26]]
    demands = [20, 18, 24, 24, 14, 25, 17, 5, 8, 11, 14, 10]
    time_windows = [[0, 303], [42, 103], [44, 131], [65, 142], [36, 129], [37, 109], [22, 82], [50, 123], [34, 108], [46, 130], [28, 103], [41, 95], [44, 132]]
    service_times = [13, 12, 13, 11, 13, 7, 11, 12, 15, 15, 5, 15]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

Subject: Delivery Routing and Scheduling with Time Windows — Operations Planning Memo

Team,

This memo defines the routing and scheduling challenge for our upcoming delivery day. We will dispatch identical vehicles from our central depot to serve all scheduled customers within defined time windows, while controlling transportation and deployment costs.

Context
- All vehicles depart the depot at time 0 and must complete a single continuous trip, returning to the depot before it closes for the day.
- Each vehicle visits a sequence of customer locations exactly once and provides unloading/service on site.
- The depot and all customer locations are specified by map coordinates. Travel time between any two points is the straight-line distance at a constant speed, so distance units and time units are aligned.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
- We must determine how many vehicles to deploy (up to the available fleet), how to assign customers to each vehicle, and in what visiting order, so that every customer is served exactly once and all returns to the depot occur before closing.
- Because all vehicles depart at the same start time, the order and grouping of customers on each route must balance travel time, waiting time, and service time to respect the latest return time at the depot.

Operational Requirements
- Time windows: Each customer has an earliest and latest acceptable start-of-service time. The vehicle’s service must begin within this window. If a vehicle arrives early, it waits until the window opens; if it would arrive after the latest time, that route plan is infeasible.
- Service times: Each stop requires a specified unloading/service duration. Departure from the customer occurs after the service is completed. If the vehicle arrived early and waited for the window to open, departure occurs at window opening plus the service time; otherwise, at arrival plus service time.
- Capacity: Vehicles have a limited carrying capacity. The total demand of all customers assigned to a vehicle cannot exceed this capacity at any point on the route.
- Single trip per vehicle: No mid-route returns, reloading, or second runs are permitted. Each vehicle leaves once at time 0, serves its assigned customers, and then returns.
- Return deadline: Each route must be planned so the vehicle returns to the depot before it closes for the day.

Cost Considerations
- Each deployed vehicle incurs a fixed cost in addition to travel distance costs. This creates a trade-off between using more vehicles to shorten routes and time slack versus limiting the fleet to reduce fixed costs.
- The planning approach should seek cost-effective clustering and sequencing of customers to reduce total distance and waiting while meeting all time and capacity constraints.

Goal
- Produce a set of routes that visit all customers exactly once, begin service within each customer’s time window, respect vehicle capacity limits, and ensure all vehicles depart at time 0 and return before the depot’s closing time.
- Minimize the total of distance-driven costs and fixed deployment costs for the vehicles used.
